title: Mapping Which Harm Categories Are Most Underprotected in Current Safety Benchmarks
original_idea: Run a standardized set of 10 prompts per harm category across 10 categories on 3 models. Measure ASR per category and compare to the category's frequency in training data proxies (e.g., SafeRLHF dataset category distribution). Identify categories with highest ASR.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Directly actionable: revealing systematic bias in safety training effort across harm categories would guide alignment teams to address underprotected areas.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Straightforward experimental design: write prompts per category, run inference, measure ASR. Comparing against training data proxies adds slight complexity. Medium compute handles 3 models easily.

narrow_scope.reasoning: 10 categories x 10 prompts x 3 models is manageable but crafting 100 quality prompts spanning 10 harm categories and sourcing training data distribution proxies broadens scope.

title: Investigating Whether Jailbreak Success Correlates with Instruction-Following Quality
original_idea: Collect instruction-following benchmark scores (e.g., MT-Bench or IFEval) and ASR on a standard jailbreak battery for 8-10 open-source models of varying sizes and training recipes. Compute the correlation coefficient between instruction-following quality and jailbreak ASR.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: High theoretical importance: if instruction-following and jailbreak susceptibility are correlated, it reveals a fundamental tension in alignment that cannot be resolved by RLHF alone. Deep implication for alignment strategy.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Requires running jailbreak batteries and collecting benchmark scores for 8-10 models. Inference on many models is time-consuming. Some published scores can be reused. Medium compute is tight for 8-10 models.

narrow_scope.reasoning: 8-10 models is ambitious for 30 hours. The core analysis (correlation) is simple, but the data collection across many models broadens scope significantly.

title: Characterizing How Jailbreak Robustness Varies Across Context Window Position
original_idea: Construct prompts where a harmful request is embedded at position 10%, 50%, and 90% of a 4K-token context window, surrounded by benign filler text. Measure ASR per position across 30 harmful prompts and 2-3 models. Include a short-context baseline.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Directly relevant: if safety weakens at certain context positions, RAG and long-document deployments are vulnerable. Clear implications for deployment defense.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Simple experimental setup: construct filler text, embed harmful request at different positions, run inference. Well within beginner CS skills. Medium compute sufficient.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Laser-focused: 3 positions, 30 prompts, 2-3 models, one variable. Very clear deliverable.

title: Measuring Whether Jailbreaks That Succeed Once Reliably Succeed on Retry
original_idea: For each of 30 harmful prompts tested with 3 attack methods on 2 models, repeat each attack attempt 10 times at temperature 1.0 and record whether each attempt succeeds. Compute per-prompt reliability (fraction of 10 attempts that succeed) and plot its distribution.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Directly informs defense design: if jailbreaks are unreliable, retry-limit defenses work; if reliable, they do not. Practical deployment implications.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Conceptually simple: run the same prompts multiple times and count successes. Requires implementing 3 attack methods, but the analysis is straightforward. Medium compute handles repeated runs.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Well-scoped: 30 prompts x 3 attacks x 2 models x 10 retries. That is 1800 inference calls, which is a lot but the experimental design is tight. Clear deliverable.

title: Replicating AILuminate Safety Scores Across Open-Source Model Families
original_idea: Run the AILuminate v1.1 public practice prompts against three or more open-source model families at comparable parameter scales. Compare hazard-category breakdowns across families and write a blog post summarizing which hazard types diverge most from proprietary baselines.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Useful for deployment decisions but primarily a replication study. The impact depends on whether interesting divergences are found. Moderate theory of change.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: AILuminate prompts are public and the framework is documented. Running inference on 3 model families at 7-13B is feasible with medium compute. Good fit for beginners.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Clear deliverable: run benchmark, compare results, write up. Scope is well-contained.

title: HELM Safety Score Replication on Multilingual Models
original_idea: Replicate HELM Safety's six risk categories on two or three multilingual open models, running prompts in at least three languages. Measure whether safety scores degrade in non-English contexts and by how much.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: High practical relevance: if safety collapses in non-English languages, globally deployed models present uncharacterized risk. Directly actionable for multilingual deployments.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Requires translating or sourcing prompts in 3+ languages and evaluating safety of non-English outputs, which is harder for beginners. Judging safety in multiple languages adds difficulty.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Multiple languages and multiple models broaden scope. Translation quality and cross-lingual evaluation add hidden complexity. Could expand beyond 30 hours.

title: TrustLLM Benchmark Results at Sub-7B Scale
original_idea: Run the TrustLLM evaluation suite on small models (Phi-3-mini, Gemma-2B, Llama-3.2-1B). Compare dimension-by-dimension (truthfulness, safety, fairness, robustness) against published 7B baselines.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Relevant for edge deployment safety but primarily a replication at smaller scale. Impact depends on whether meaningful differences are found.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: TrustLLM suite is open source, small models fit on consumer hardware. Straightforward to run and compare. Good beginner project.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Run existing benchmark on 3 small models, compare against published baselines. Clear, contained scope.

title: SimpleQA Factual Accuracy Replication Across Model Generations
original_idea: Run SimpleQA on models from three successive generations (e.g., Llama-2, Llama-3, Llama-3.1). Disaggregate scores by topic domain and compute per-domain improvement curves to identify areas of persistent failure.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Factual accuracy is related to safety (hallucination) but the connection is indirect. Identifying domain-specific hallucination patterns is useful but not a direct safety intervention.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: SimpleQA has ground-truth answers, making evaluation straightforward. Running 3 model generations is feasible. Good beginner project.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Run one benchmark on 3 models, disaggregate by domain. Well-defined deliverable.

title: Replicating HELM Safety Across Code-Specialized Models
original_idea: Apply HELM Safety's violence, fraud, harassment, and deception categories to three code models. Compare safety profiles against matched general-purpose models and analyze whether code-tuning degrades safety alignment.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Code models are used in agentic pipelines and can execute harmful code. Finding a safety gap specific to code-tuned models would directly motivate targeted mitigations.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: HELM Safety framework is accessible, code models are open source and comparably sized. Straightforward comparison. Beginner-friendly.

narrow_scope.reasoning: 3 code models vs. 3 general models on one benchmark. Clear scope and deliverable.

title: Cross-Benchmark Correlation Study: AILuminate vs. HELM Safety
original_idea: Evaluate five to seven open-source models on both AILuminate public prompts and HELM Safety. Compute rank correlations and identify models that rank highly on one but poorly on the other. Analyze which hazard categories explain divergences.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: If leading benchmarks produce inconsistent rankings, it reveals a fundamental reliability problem for safety evaluation. Important meta-level finding.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Running 5-7 models on two full benchmarks is compute-intensive and time-consuming. Correlation analysis itself is simple. Medium compute may be stretched.

narrow_scope.reasoning: 5-7 models on 2 benchmarks is ambitious for 30 hours. Could be narrowed to 3 models but as stated it is broad.

title: Safety Benchmark Performance Under Quantization
original_idea: Take three models (e.g., Mistral-7B, Llama-3-8B, Phi-3-medium), run AILuminate or HELM Safety on the full-precision and 4-bit quantized versions, and measure safety score deltas relative to capability (MMLU) score deltas.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: If quantization degrades safety disproportionately to capability, this is a direct, actionable finding for deployment practice.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Quantization tools are well-documented, benchmark frameworks are public. Running both versions is straightforward. Good fit for medium compute.

narrow_scope.reasoning: 3 models, 2 precisions each, 1-2 benchmarks. Clear comparison with defined deliverable.

title: Replicating ForesightSafety Bench on Instruction-Tuned vs. Base Models
original_idea: Run ForesightSafety Bench on base and instruction-tuned variants of the same model family (e.g., Llama-3-8B-base vs. Llama-3-8B-Instruct). Analyze which bench categories improve with instruction tuning and which do not.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: If instruction tuning does not improve anticipatory safety reasoning, it exposes a limitation of RLHF-based alignment. Meaningful finding for alignment research.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Matched base/instruct pairs are freely available. Running a benchmark on 2 model variants is simple. Beginner-friendly.

narrow_scope.reasoning: One benchmark, one model family, base vs. instruct comparison. Extremely focused.

title: Safety Score Replication Across Prompt Formats (Chat vs. Completion)
original_idea: Convert AILuminate prompts to completion format (no system prompt, no conversation structure) and run them against models evaluated in their standard chat format. Measure how much safety scores shift.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: If completion format bypasses alignment mechanisms, this is directly actionable for API providers and developers who use raw completions.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Simple transformation (strip chat formatting) and run inference. Very accessible for beginners.

narrow_scope.reasoning: One variable (prompt format), existing prompts, clear deliverable. Extremely narrow and well-defined.

title: METR Task Suite Performance Replication Across Open-Source Agents
original_idea: Run a subset of publicly available METR tasks on two or three open-source agentic frameworks. Compare task completion rates, safety failures, and instruction hierarchy violations against published proprietary baselines.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Characterizing safety gaps in open-source agents is useful but primarily descriptive. Moderate impact on safety practice.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Setting up agentic frameworks (AutoGPT, OpenDevin) and running METR tasks requires significant configuration effort. Agentic evaluations are complex. Challenging for beginners.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Agentic evaluations involve many moving parts (framework setup, task configuration, evaluation criteria). Likely exceeds 30 hours.

title: Safety Benchmark Sensitivity to System Prompt Wording
original_idea: Evaluate three models on AILuminate using five systematically varied system prompts (varying strictness, persona, and topic framing). Compute variance in safety scores across system prompt variants and identify categories with highest sensitivity.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: If safety benchmark scores are highly sensitive to system prompt wording, leaderboard rankings are unreliable. Directly undermines confidence in safety evaluations.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Very simple: write 5 system prompts, run AILuminate on 3 models with each, compute variance. Minimal technical skills required. Perfect for beginners.

narrow_scope.reasoning: 3 models, 5 system prompts, 1 benchmark. Clear, tight scope with a single variable under study.
